Welcome to Wellesley Park Primary School
Welcome to Wellesley Park Primary School
Wellesley Park Primary School is proud to be part of the Blackdown Education Partnership, working alongside a family of schools across Somerset and Devon.
At Wellesley Park, we believe that a happy child is a successful child. Our school is a warm, welcoming community where every child is known, valued, and supported to thrive. We nurture individual strengths and talents, and we’re committed to providing a rich and inclusive education that inspires curiosity, confidence, and a lifelong love of learning.
We are incredibly proud that the dedication of our staff was recognised by Ofsted. Visitors consistently comment on the strong relationships between staff and pupils, and the way children are encouraged to ‘have a go’, build resilience, and take pride in their learning.
“Pupils feel welcomed, known and supported from the moment they arrive at Wellesley Park. They enjoy school, feel safe and are proud to be part of the school community. High expectations, strong relationships and a commitment to helping every child succeed enable pupils to thrive both academically and personally.” — Ofsted Report, 2026
We are deeply committed to creating a safe, nurturing environment where children feel secure, supported, and ready to learn. Our safeguarding culture is embedded across the school, with strong systems in place and a dedicated team working closely with families and external agencies to ensure the highest standards of care and wellbeing.
We understand the vital role a primary school plays in a child’s life - not just academically, but emotionally and socially. Our aim is to create positive learning experiences and lasting memories for both children and their families.
We would be delighted to welcome you to Wellesley Park Primary School. If you have any questions or would like to arrange a visit, please don’t hesitate to contact our school office.
Contact
Feel free to contact us with any questions.Emailoffice@wellesleypark.bep.ac

pageCache.pageTitle: Vision & Values — Wellesley Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
Vision & Values
Our Vision and Values
At Wellesley Park, we are committed to fostering an inclusive and nurturing environment where every child is valued and encouraged to reach their full potential. Our mission, "Belief in Every Child,". We believe that every child has unique talents and abilities, and it is our responsibility to provide the support and opportunities they need to thrive.
Resilience: We encourage our pupils to persevere through challenges and develop a strong sense of determination.
Respect: We cultivate a culture of mutual respect, where every member of our school community is valued and heard.
Responsibility: We promote accountability and responsibility in all our actions and decisions.
Tolerance: We celebrate diversity and foster an environment of understanding and acceptance.
Integrity: We uphold honesty, responsibility, and 'doing the right thing' at all times.
Excellence: We strive for excellence in all aspects of education, encouraging pupils to achieve their best academically, creatively, and personally.
We are dedicated to providing a well-rounded education that not only focuses on academic achievement but also on the holistic development of each child. Through a rich and varied curriculum, extracurricular activities, and a supportive learning environment, we aim to inspire a lifelong love of learning and prepare our pupils for future success.
At Wellesley Park, we truly believe in every child and are committed to helping them discover and develop their unique strengths and passions.

pageCache.pageTitle: School News — Wellesley Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
Nursery
Nursery
Welcome to our nursery, which is a part of Wellesley Park Primary School. Our aim is to provide a welcoming, friendly and safe setting, where your child can flourish. We intend to support all children in developing important skills that will set them on the road for a happy and successful life. We offer care and education to children aged from 9 months old until Reception age.
Our setting provides the children with a stimulating environment within which to learn, with large open spaces to explore whilst also providing cosy areas to feel safe and secure. Our team of highly skilled practitioners work closely with our children and their families to develop trusting relationships and to support children in their learning.
At Wellesley Park Explorers we share the same vision and value of the school: Belief in Every Child, and is at the heart of everything we do.
Children’s self-confidence is nurtured as a priority from the early years. Interactions and the relationships established between practitioners and children consistently reinforce this approach across the nursery. Children are encouraged to ‘have a go’ and become active in their own learning.
Our prospectus will give you lots of information that you need to decide whether Wellesley Park Explorers is the right setting for your child. However, we know that often the best way to know this is to visit us! We encourage you to ring and arrange a visit to come and see our high-quality provision for yourself.
For all telephone enquiries please call: 01823 666814
You can also contact us via email: explorers@wellesleypark.bep.ac
We look forward to meeting you.
Learning through play and our curriculum
The nursery at Wellesley Park Explorers has dedicated rooms and outdoor space accommodated within the grounds of Wellesley Park School. It has been designed to create a stimulating, nurturing and safe environment where young children can play, make friends and grow in confidence. Your child will learn about themselves, each other and their wider world, through purposeful play activities. Reading, writing and maths are important aspects of our nursery curriculum, tailored to meet your child’s needs. At Wellesley Park Explorers, special attention is paid to your child’s emotional wellbeing, where each child learns about feelings and emotions through stories, circle time and imaginative play.
Each child is allocated a key worker who will be there to support your child on a more personal level – emotionally, socially, physically and academically – as well as being your point of contact with our nursery.
Please be advised admission to Wellesley Park Explorers does not guarantee a place at Wellesley Park Primary School. The normal school admission process applies for admission to Wellesley Park Primary School. Parents/carers will still need to apply for a place in the reception year at school at the appropriate time.
Wellesley Park EYFS Curriculum Overview Birth to Five
Key Information
Starting from September 2025, our nursery will be open from 7:30am to 6:00pm, Monday to Friday, all year round. We are proud to offer both term-time only and year-round care, with a variety of flexible sessions designed to meet the needs of busy families. Our aim is to provide affordable, high-quality childcare that fits around your schedule.
We follow the 0-5 Early Years Foundation Stage Curriculum, which has seven areas of learning and development:
Personal and Social Development
Communication and Language
Understanding of the World
Physical Development
Expressive Arts and Design
There are several forms of funding available:
Universal Funding: All children who turn three are eligible for 15 hours of Universal funding as from the term after their third birthday.
Extended funding (also known as 30-hour funding)- If you would like to apply for 30-hour funding you would need to submit your application & have received your 11-digit code the term prior to when you would like to access it. 30 hours free childcare - Homepage | HMRC Childcare Choices
Funding for 2 year olds for working families:The Government have introduced 15 hours of free childcare for all two-year-olds with working parents, this funding can be accessed via Homepage | HMRC Childcare Choices.
Funding for 2 year olds:Funding is available for families who meet eligibility criteria Funding for 2-year-olds (somerset.gov.uk)
For further information, please see our Fees Policy.
Expression of Interest
Would you like some more information about Wellesley Park Preschool? Perhaps you would like to come and take a look at out wonderful setting? If so, please fill in the 'Expression of Interest' form and we'll get back to you as soon as possible - Expression of Interest Form.

pageCache.text:
September 2026 Starters
Welcome to Wellesley Park Primary School
Belief in Every Child
We are delighted to welcome you and your child to Wellesley Park Primary School as part of our new Reception cohort. We know this is a very special and exciting time for both children and parents, and we are very much looking forward to meeting you all.
Starting school is a significant milestone, and it is natural for children to need time to settle into this new experience. Your child may experience a range of emotions, please be reassured that all of these feelings are completely normal.
At Wellesley Park, we believe that happiness is the key to success. Our children learn within a happy, caring environment where individual needs are recognised and talents are nurtured. Our aim is that all children experience success throughout their primary years. To support this, we set high expectations that enable our children to reach their full potential across all areas of the curriculum, while also preparing them for the wider world beyond the classroom.
As a school, we place great importance on children’s wellbeing, recognising it as the foundation for effective learning. Below, you will find a range of helpful resources which we encourage you to explore. These are designed to support both you and your child in feeling confident about starting school and to help ease any questions or anxieties you may have.
Helping to get your child ready for school
New Parent presentation - June 2026
Hot School Meals
When Does My Child Start?
Application forms for Universal Free School Meals will be included in your welcome pack and sent to all parents and carers. Completing this form entitles your child to free hot school meals throughout Reception, Year 1 and Year 2.
We encourage all families to return the form, even if you do not think your child will initially choose hot school dinners, as this keeps the option available should you change your mind later. Once completed, please return the form to the school office.
School meals for Reception children will begin on Wednesday 9th September. Further details on how to book meals will be shared as part of your welcome pack.
From w/c 21st September 2026, you will be able to select your child’s meal choices via our school management system, Arbor. Further details about accessing and using Arbor will be shared with you in due course.
The Autumn term will begin on Monday 7th September 2026. Please see the transition letter for further details.
School term dates are available on our website under Parents → Term Dates.
Further information, including school uniform, daily timings, procedures for illness, guidance on administering medicine, and other helpful details, will also be shared in the new starter information packs.
We are looking forward to welcoming you and your child to Wellesley Park Primary School as they start their learning journey with us.

Our Partners
The School is actively involved in a number of high quality partnerships that help us play our part both within the education world and within the local community.
Westcountry Training School Alliance
The West Country Training School Alliance (WCTSA) is a vibrant and diverse partnership of schools working across Devon and Somerset to create a sustainable and powerful system for school improvement.

Inspired Schools
Inspired Schools provides a range of outstanding physical education coaching services to Primary Schools within Somerset.

pageCache.pageTitle: Personal Development — Wellesley Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
Personal Development
At Wellesley Park Primary School, we place a great emphasis on the Personal Development of our children as we feel this is every bit as important as their academic performance.
Today's children and young people are growing up in an increasingly complex world and living their lives seamlessly on and offline. This presents many positive and exciting opportunities, but also challenges and risks. In this environment, children and young people need to know how to be safe and healthy, and how to manage their academic, personal and social lives in a positive way.
At our school, Personal Development has six main themes:
Spiritual, Moral, Social & Cultural Development
Relationship & Health Education (including PSHE)
Physical Development
Below you will find our Personal Development Booklet, which outlines how Wellesley Park Primary School nurtures the whole child through a rich programme of values education, wellbeing support, cultural enrichment, physical development, and wider opportunities that help every pupil grow academically, socially, and personally.
Personal Development Booklet
PSHE
Assemblies
British Values
Enrichment
Houses
Equality and Diversity
We provide our children with a high-quality PSHE curriculum through Jigsaw PSHE. Every child has specific PSHE lessons each week as well as circle time and other opportunities to discuss personal, social and health matters. In Nursery and Reception, PSHE is part of the PSED prime area of learning as children are provided with the necessary skills they need to build relationships, discuss and understand their emotions and learn personal hygiene skills.
Assemblies are an important aspect of our Personal Development curriculum. They give us an opportunity to discuss our school values and attributes as a collective so that children are able to see the importance that these have on our daily lives. We are also able to address areas of the PSHE curriculum that are pertinent to all children such as NSPCC PANTS, online safety and anti-bullying. Through our assemblies we are also able to highlight and teach children about British Values. We are also able to celebrate our achievements.
British Values enable children to feel part of a community and understand the country that we live in more. The values allow the children to develop their character and become effective citizens. We cover the British Values in our assemblies and ensure that there is clear understanding of the vocabulary. We also learn about them through our Picture News lessons where children learn more about the world we live in and are able to see the British Values in a context.
British Values are an important part of learning about equality and diversity. We want to ensure that our children understand how diverse our country is and why the British Values are important.
Another aspect of our Personal Development curriculum is the opportunities that we provide the children. We want to make sure that the children are presented with as diverse a range of experiences as possible to ensure that they have the cultural capital to make informed choices and to be successful and happy in the future. We ensure that there are trips planned into our curriculum, for example, visits to the theatre to see a pantomime and a trip to London. We invite visitors into our school to enrich our curriculum. We also provide children with a range of activities within school to enhance the children’s learning.
Extra Curricular
Community
Alongside enrichment within school, we also provide extracurricular opportunities for our children. There is a wide range of clubs available to children from Reception onwards. Please see our current Extra Curricular timetable.
As well as chosen extracurricular clubs, we also provide targeted clubs to those children who require extra support with areas of the curriculum. This may take the form of specific clubs such as phonics club before school.
We want our children to feel part of a community within school, whether that is through being part of their class or through membership of clubs or councils. We have a school council who has an impact on developments and decisions within the school. We also have an Eco School Council who ensure that the school is doing everything that it can for the environment – recycling, litter picking in the local area, reducing our energy consumption and building habitats for insects.
We also have a PTA group who fundraise for the school and provide brilliant opportunities for the school and community such as seasonal fairs, family discos and pre-loved book fairs. Events involve staff, families and community members which links to our values of belonging and participating.
In addition to this, we also have strong links with the community through events with the local library, the local churches and the town council, Rotary Club and Dementia Care home. This helps us with our curriculum but also ensures that our school and families feel like an important part of Wellington itself.
As part of our school community, each child belongs to one of our four houses: Blackdown, Exmoor, Mendip and Quantock. Our houses ensure every child belongs and has a sense of worth, through participation.
Equality and Diversity is integral to our Personal Development curriculum. Across the subject areas, knowledge is chosen to highlight equality and diversity at every opportunity. Our resources are chosen carefully to reflect the diverse nature of this country. We celebrate diversity, whether this is through the different languages spoken by children and staff or studying and celebrating world celebrations and festivals to ensure acceptance and tolerance.

Admissions
Wellesley Park Primary School is a member of the Blackdown Education Partnership which is the admitting authority, responsible for the admissions policies and decisions on applications for admission. We have an admissions policy for each academic year. They are written to comply with the School Admissions Code and School Admissions Appeals Code.
Applications to Wellesley Park Primary School should be made through Somerset Council and will be considered in accordance with the arrangements set out in the co-ordinated admissions scheme for primary schools in Somerset.

Curriculum Overview
Our Curriculum
At Wellesley Park, our curriculum is thoughtfully designed to reflect our vision and values, ensuring that every child receives a comprehensive and enriching education. Guided by our mission, "Belief in Every Child," we aim to provide a curriculum that not only meets academic standards but also fosters personal growth and development.
Our Curriculum Statement
Our curriculum is built on five key pillars that reflect our commitment to providing a comprehensive and enriching educational experience for all pupils. These pillars guide our approach to teaching and learning, ensuring that every child has the opportunity to thrive academically, socially, and personally.
1.Subject Knowledge: We prioritise a deep understanding of substantive knowledge across all disciplines.
Substantive knowledge is crucial for several reasons:
Foundation for Learning: It provides the essential facts and information that form the basis of understanding in any subject. For example, in history, knowing key events and figures helps pupils grasp the broader context of historical developments.
Building Blocks for Higher-Order Thinking: Substantive knowledge allows pupils to engage in more complex cognitive processes, such as analysis and evaluation. Without a solid foundation of facts, it's challenging to develop critical thinking skills.
Retention and Application: Knowledge that is well-organised and deeply understood is more likely to be retained and applied in different contexts. This helps pupils make connections between different areas of learning and apply their knowledge.
Confidence and Competence: Mastery of substantive knowledge boosts pupils' confidence in their abilities and encourages a positive attitude towards learning. It enables them to participate more fully in discussions and activities.
Preparation for Future Learning: A strong base of substantive knowledge prepares pupils for more the next stage of their education and lifelong learning
2. Cognitive Science: Our teaching methods are informed by the latest research in cognitive science, ensuring that our children benefit from evidence-based practices. We focus on how pupils learn best, incorporating strategies that enhance memory, understanding, and critical thinking.
3. Pedagogy: Effective pedagogy is at the heart of our curriculum. We employ a variety of teaching approaches to meet the diverse needs of our pupils, ensuring that every child is engaged and challenged. Our teachers are committed to continuous professional development, staying abreast of the latest educational research and best practices to deliver high-quality instruction.
4. Reading: Reading is a fundamental skill that underpins all areas of learning. We place a strong emphasis on developing proficient and enthusiastic readers. Our curriculum includes a rich and diverse range of texts, fostering a love of reading and promoting literacy across the curriculum.
5. Personal Development: We believe in nurturing the whole child, supporting their personal development alongside their academic growth. Our curriculum includes opportunities for pupils to develop social and emotional skills, resilience, and a sense of responsibility. We provide a range of extracurricular activities and enrichment programs that encourage pupils to explore their interests and develop their talents.
In summary, we are dedicated to providing a curriculum that is both rigorous and supportive, preparing our children for success in an ever-changing world. We believe in every child's potential and are committed to helping them discover and develop their unique strengths and passions.
Enrichment and Extra Curricular Activities
Enrichment and extracurricular clubs are a key focus at Wellesley Park. The activities we offer provide children with the opportunity to explore new interests, develop essential skills, and build lasting friendships. From art and music clubs that ignite creativity, to Lego and coding clubs that encourage problem-solving and critical thinking, there's something for every child. Sports clubs promote physical fitness and teamwork, while wellbeing clubs support children with resilience and mindfulness. Participation in these clubs not only enhances academic performance but also boosts confidence and social skills. These engaging activities contribute to a vibrant and inclusive school community where every child can thrive.

Preparation for Future Learning: A strong base of substantive knowledge prepares pupils for more the next stage of their education and lifelong learning
2. Cognitive Science: Our teaching methods are informed by the latest research in cognitive science, ensuring that our children benefit from evidence-based practices. We focus on how pupils learn best, incorporating strategies that enhance memory, understanding, and critical thinking.
3. Pedagogy: Effective pedagogy is at the heart of our curriculum. We employ a variety of teaching approaches to meet the diverse needs of our pupils, ensuring that every child is engaged and challenged. Our teachers are committed to continuous professional development, staying abreast of the latest educational research and best practices to deliver high-quality instruction.
4. Reading: Reading is a fundamental skill that underpins all areas of learning. We place a strong emphasis on developing proficient and enthusiastic readers. Our curriculum includes a rich and diverse range of texts, fostering a love of reading and promoting literacy across the curriculum.
5. Personal Development: We believe in nurturing the whole child, supporting their personal development alongside their academic growth. Our curriculum includes opportunities for pupils to develop social and emotional skills, resilience, and a sense of responsibility. We provide a range of extracurricular activities and enrichment programs that encourage pupils to explore their interests and develop their talents.
In summary, we are dedicated to providing a curriculum that is both rigorous and supportive, preparing our children for success in an ever-changing world. We believe in every child's potential and are committed to helping them discover and develop their unique strengths and passions.
Enrichment and Extra Curricular Activities
Enrichment and extracurricular clubs are a key focus at Wellesley Park. The activities we offer provide children with the opportunity to explore new interests, develop essential skills, and build lasting friendships. From art and music clubs that ignite creativity, to Lego and coding clubs that encourage problem-solving and critical thinking, there's something for every child. Sports clubs promote physical fitness and teamwork, while wellbeing clubs support children with resilience and mindfulness. Participation in these clubs not only enhances academic performance but also boosts confidence and social skills. These engaging activities contribute to a vibrant and inclusive school community where every child can thrive.

British Values
In accordance with the Department for Education we aim to actively promote British values in school to ensure young people leave school prepared for life in modern Britain. At Wellesley Park Primary, these values are reinforced regularly by focusing on the following:
At Wellesley Park Primary children have many opportunities for their voices to be heard. We have a school council which meets regularly to discuss issues raised in class council meetings is able to genuinely effect change within the school.
The importance of laws, whether they be those that govern the class, the school, or the country, are consistently reinforced throughout regular school days, as well as when dealing with behaviour and through school assemblies. Children are taught the value and reasons behind laws, that they govern and protect us, the responsibilities that this involves and the consequences when laws are broken.
Within school, children are actively encouraged to make choices, knowing that they are in a safe and supportive environment. As a school we educate and provide boundaries for young children to make choices safely, through provision of a safe environment and empowering education. Children are encouraged to know, understand and exercise their rights and personal freedoms and are advised how to exercise these safely, for example through our e-Safety and PSHE lessons.
Mutual respect is at the heart of Wellesley Park values. Children learn that their behaviours have an effect on their own rights and those of others. All members of the school community treat each other with respect.
Tolerance of those of Different Faiths and Beliefs
Wellesley Park Primary is situated in an area which has a mixture of fantastic cultural diversity and we place a great emphasis on promoting diversity with the children. Assemblies will be regularly planned to celebrate and promote a variety of faiths and cultures. At Wellesley Park Primary we will actively challenge children, staff and parents/carers expressing opinions contrary to fundamental British Values, including ‘extremist’ views.
The purpose of the Wellesley Park Primary ‘Prevent Strategy’ is to protect children from harm and to ensure that they are taught in a way that is consistent with the law and British values. To this end it will act to;
Enable learners to make a positive contribution
Safeguard young people

Nursery
Nursery
Welcome to our nursery, which is a part of Wellesley Park Primary School. Our aim is to provide a welcoming, friendly and safe setting, where your child can flourish. We intend to support all children in developing important skills that will set them on the road for a happy and successful life. We offer care and education to children aged from 9 months old until Reception age.
Our setting provides the children with a stimulating environment within which to learn, with large open spaces to explore whilst also providing cosy areas to feel safe and secure. Our team of highly skilled practitioners work closely with our children and their families to develop trusting relationships and to support children in their learning.
At Wellesley Park Explorers we share the same vision and value of the school: Belief in Every Child, and is at the heart of everything we do.
Children’s self-confidence is nurtured as a priority from the early years. Interactions and the relationships established between practitioners and children consistently reinforce this approach across the nursery. Children are encouraged to ‘have a go’ and become active in their own learning.
Our prospectus will give you lots of information that you need to decide whether Wellesley Park Explorers is the right setting for your child. However, we know that often the best way to know this is to visit us! We encourage you to ring and arrange a visit to come and see our high-quality provision for yourself.
For all telephone enquiries please call: 01823 666814
You can also contact us via email: explorers@wellesleypark.bep.ac
We look forward to meeting you.
Learning through play and our curriculum
The nursery at Wellesley Park Explorers has dedicated rooms and outdoor space accommodated within the grounds of Wellesley Park School. It has been designed to create a stimulating, nurturing and safe environment where young children can play, make friends and grow in confidence. Your child will learn about themselves, each other and their wider world, through purposeful play activities. Reading, writing and maths are important aspects of our nursery curriculum, tailored to meet your child’s needs. At Wellesley Park Explorers, special attention is paid to your child’s emotional wellbeing, where each child learns about feelings and emotions through stories, circle time and imaginative play.
Each child is allocated a key worker who will be there to support your child on a more personal level – emotionally, socially, physically and academically – as well as being your point of contact with our nursery.
Please be advised admission to Wellesley Park Explorers does not guarantee a place at Wellesley Park Primary School. The normal school admission process applies for admission to Wellesley Park Primary School. Parents/carers will still need to apply for a place in the reception year at school at the appropriate time.
